key_terms.الْمُصَدَّقَةُ عَلَى نَفْسِهَا: The one who ratifies/testifies for herself

ai.seo_question: Can a woman marry without a guardian if she testifies she is unmarried?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the principle of 'self-validation' (al-muṣaddaqah ‘alā nafsihā) in Shia jurisprudence, where a woman’s testimony regarding her marital status suffices in the absence of a guardian (wali). It underscores the flexibility of marriage contracts in early Islamic society, particularly in remote contexts where formal witnesses were unavailable, relying instead on the woman's direct declaration. This ruling is foundational for understanding the conditions under which a marriage is considered valid without the explicit consent or presence of the female party's male guardian.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Fazalat Bin Ayoub, from Umar Bin Aban Al Kalby, from Maysarat who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘I meet a woman in the wilderness wherein there is no one, so I am saying to her, ‘Is there a husband for you?’ So she is saying, ‘No’. Can I marry her?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, she is the ratified one upon herself’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from ‘Umar ibn Aban al-Kalbiy from Maysarah who has said the following:

“This is concerning my question before abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a woman whom I meet in the wilderness and I ask her if she has a husband and she says, ‘No; I do not have a husband’ if I can marry her. He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, her words about herself are accepted as true.’”
